host_validation.limitations: Complete native power shutdown/internal SoC shutdown/reinit and a bounded post-disable section execute against modeled CDS/parent-stop/probe/IRQ primitives. The native post-disable call now invokes production host preparation and qualified reclamation. SSR qualification results and later parent/probe operations remain models; no fake CDS callback performs retirement. Sticky private failure has no retry/reset API; this is failure admission/propagation, not a complete recovery coordinator. Physical remove/close is unchanged. Complete native adapter-reset function executes with modeled held-safe iterator, one active link per adapter, queue/scan/WMM/TWT/TDLS/stop primitives and VDEV references. No real SSR timing, kernel iterator concurrency, adapter-stop bodies or native parent teardown is certified by this reset fixture. Real helper C and extracted factory/rollback fragments with simulated HDD and synchronization. Complete native idle shutdown executes against modeled psoc synchronization, event and module-stop calls. SSR batch is a result/ownership model here; actual runtime batch, recovery policy and native callbacks are exercised by the separate existing runtime fixtures. The ordinary-idle coordinator executes production C against modeled runtime return values and synchronization; real native runtime destruction is covered separately, not end-to-end with this host here. This does not certify SSR/remove or prepared/UP recovery. Registry mutexes model spinlocks. Device and object-manager reference primitives are models; this validates host pin ownership and identity admission, not physical native parent deletion. Allocation pins do not preserve HDD, native components or firmware. Caller must retain and serialize complete parent lifetime across polls. The explicit handed-off SSR poll delegates qualification to the existing bridge and modeled batch here; actual batch policy/native cleanup have separate fixtures. Native SSR post-disable now reaches the qualified bridge; automatic async continuation and physical-remove coordination remain unconnected. This does not certify native kernel locking, teardown or radio validation.
